title: JsonCase
description:
The whole case file. `$schema` is accepted and ignored - it points a
human's editor at [`emit_schema`]'s output, and carries no information the
reader needs.

chemistry.description: SPEC-LIT §137.2: the mechanism, the thermo set and the integrator.

dust.description:
SPEC-LIT §157.4: the `dust` block (`crate::io::case_dust`), the
DST-06 equivalent-gas charge beside a `combustion.model` FSC/TFC.
Absent (the default) is every case this reader has ever built;
present, it lowers to [`LoweredCase::dust`] and every driver but
`ofgpu-lowmach` refuses the case by name.

motion.description:
SPEC-LIT 105.12: a prescribed motion of the mesh's points. Absent (the
default) is every case this reader has ever built; a case without it
lowers, serialises and runs exactly as before.

parcels.description:
SPEC-LIT §137.2: the parcel model (`crate::io::case_parcels`). Absent
(the default) is every case this reader has ever built; present, it
lowers to [`LoweredCase::parcels`] and every driver refuses the case
until CHR-26 wires `ofgpu-lowmach` (§137.6).

patches.description:
ORDERED, matched first-to-last - section 4.1 point 1. A JSON object's
keys cannot carry this, which is the entire reason this is an array of
`{match, ...}` records rather than a `{"pattern": {...}}` map.

sources.description:
SPEC-LIT §18/§31: volumetric sources. Empty (the default) is every
case this reader has ever built. See [`JsonSource`] for what a JSONC
case can say that the OpenFOAM `constant/fvSources` route
([`crate::sources::read_sources`]) cannot express and vice versa.

species.description:
SPEC-LIT §137.2: the species set (`crate::io::case_chem`). Absent
(the default) is every case this reader has ever built; present, the
three blocks lower to [`LoweredCase::chem`] and every driver refuses
the case until CHR-12b wires `ofgpu-lowmach` (§137.7).

vent.description:
SPEC-LIT §158.8: the one-domain opening vent (DST-09). Absent is every
case this reader has built; present, it lowers to
[`LoweredCase::vent`] and every driver but `ofgpu-compressible`
refuses the case by name.

BuoyancyModel.description:
The two body-force forms a case can name - SPEC-LIT §9's density ratio
and §121's Boussinesq, lowered through
[`crate::momentum::BuoyancyForm::lower`]. `boussinesq` runs when the case
carries a `beta` for it (§121.7); see [`Self::name`] for the spelling the
lowering contract hands on.

JsonBoundaries.description:
Which patch each of the six box faces belongs to, `-x +x -y +y -z +z` -
[`crate::blockgen::BlockSpec`]'s own slot order.

atol.description: The absolute tolerance of every mass fraction.

mechanism.description: The CHEMKIN mechanism, relative to the case.

thermo.description: The CHEMKIN thermo file, relative to the case.

transport.description: A TRAN file. Refused: the Lewis route reads none (§137.2).

A.description: kg/(m2 s Pa), A of R_kin.

C0.description: kg/(m s Pa K^0.75), C_0 of R_diff.

hc.description:
J/kg, the heat per kg of carbon burnt; absent is ISL22's 32.9 MJ/kg
(§159.1).

B.description: EDM's `B`; absent removes the product-limiting argument.

PrT.description:
FSC/TFC's Pr_t (§151.5: each case its own - Leeds 0.4, REMBE 0.28).
REQUIRED with `model` FSC or TFC; there is no default.

flameAge.description:
`global` (the default, the papers' clock of (154.2)) or `local` (the
transported flame age of SPEC-LIT §160.5); FSC only - refused with
TFC, which has no clock.

ignition.description: The ignition source of (155.4); absent is no ignition source.

maxFlameCourant.description:
The flame-Courant limit Co_f,max of (155.9); the default is
`ofgpu::dust::courant::CO_F_MAX` = 0.5.

model.description:
`laminar` (the default) | `EDM` | `EDC` | `PaSR` | `FSC` | `TFC`.
`FSC` and `TFC` are the dust model's closures (§154); they lower in
`crate::io::case_dust` and are refused here, as is every one of the
four keys below under any of the four species-closure names.

prescribedUt.description:
Gate DST-VES's prescribed `U_t` (SPEC-LIT §157.6): the TFC operator
runs at `U_t = S0 (T_u/T_u0)^alpha (p/p0)^beta` instead of the
closures'. TFC only - refused beside `model` FSC and beside any
turbulence model, and lowered in `crate::io::case_dust`.

tFlacc.description:
The extended FSC's t_flacc (§154.7). FSC only - TFC has no clock
(§154.6).

tauChem.description: PaSR's chemical time by name (§134.4). No default.

tauMix.description: PaSR's mixing time by name (§134.4). No default.

unburnedDensity.description:
Gate DST-VES's density the propagation reads (SPEC-LIT §157.6):
`"compressed"` (the default, the (155.10) gas) or `"initial"` - the
negative control of INSIGHTS (g). Lowered in `crate::io::case_dust`.

JsonComposition.description: `dust.cloud.composition` - the four stage fractions of one particle.

char.description: The char's share (`char` is a legal field name).

JsonCompressible.description:
`physics.compressible` - SPEC-LIT §122.6, the JSONC statement of §122.1's
gas: `gamma` and `W` state it, a stated `cp` must agree with (122.5) to
`1e-6` relative, `Pr` defaults to 0.71, and `pOperating` (§122.2's
`p_op`, Pa) has no default.

cp.description: J/(kg K); checked against (122.5), never used in its place.

vapour.description:
The species that receives the vapour; required with `mass
evaporation`, and one of `species.names`.

JsonCyclicPair.description:
One `mesh.cyclic[]` entry - SPEC-LIT §31.1. `a` and `b` are two of the six
`mesh.boundaries` values, and must name the two opposite slots of one
axis (`xmin`/`xmax`, `ymin`/`ymax` or `zmin`/`zmax`) - `build_block`
checks that, not this type.

`transform` takes only `"translate"` - the transform
[`crate::blockgen::BlockSpec::set_cyclic_axis`] knows how to build a
pairing from, implied by the block's own extent along that axis. A
rotational pair (`"rotate"`, with an axis and an angle) needs a different
face-matching search and a vector transform on `Sf` that nothing here
implements yet, so it deserialises fine (it is a *known* setting) and is
refused in `build_block` with a SPEC-LIT §13.4 error naming `translate` -
exactly like any other recognised-but-unimplemented setting, not a parse
failure.

JsonDisplacement.description: A displacement from the rest position, tagged on `kind`.

JsonDust.description:
The `dust` block (SPEC-LIT §157.4). `thermo` names one of §152.9's two
modes; the keys each mode reads are refused on the other. Required in a
Phase A case; a case stating a `cloud` states none of the Phase A keys,
`thermo` included (§159.9).

SL.description:
m/s, the laminar burning velocity. REQUIRED in the prescribed mode;
in the formula mode omitted is (152.13)'s S_L(phi).

Tb.description: K, the measured burned temperature (Leeds 1500); prescribed only.

Wb.description: kg/mol, the burned molar mass (Leeds 0.0297); prescribed only.

Wu.description: kg/mol, the unburned molar mass (Leeds 0.0328); prescribed only.

cloud.description:
The reacting dust cloud (SPEC-LIT §159.9, DST-14); `None` for every
Phase A case. Beside `combustion.model` FSC or TFC it is refused:
Phase B burns the volatile on the finite-rate path, and Phase A's
equivalent gas would count the same fuel twice.

cp.description: J/(kg K), the one c_p both pseudo-species carry; prescribed only.

phi.description:
The equivalence ratio (152.2); REQUIRED in the formula mode, refused
in the prescribed one. Held as the exact fraction of the decimal the
case wrote.

sst.description:
The ρ-weighted SST's settings (§156.3, §156.4); refused without
turbulence.model kOmegaSST.

thermo.description:
`formula` (the pseudo-species of (152.1)-(152.8) at phi) |
`prescribed` (one constant c_p, §152.9). Required in a Phase A case
(refused by name when absent there) and refused beside a `cloud`;
optional in the schema only so a cloud can stand without it
(SPEC-LIT §159.9).

JsonDustCloud.description:
`dust.cloud` (SPEC-LIT §159.9): the uniform reacting dust cloud DST-14
states and lowers, DST-15 runs. The size is exactly one of `diameter`
and `rosinRammler`. The GAS side of [`ParticleInputs`] is not the
cloud's - [`LoweredCloud::particle_inputs`] takes it from the caller,
which in DST-15 is the gas.

char.description: The char reaction (159.5); only with char > 0, absent is inert.

composition.description: The four stage fractions; each in [0, 1], the sum within 1e-9 of 1.

concentration.description: kg/m3, the cloud's mass per gas volume; finite and above zero.

cpP.description: J/(kg K), the one c_p of (159.1) for the whole particle.

devolatilisation.description:
SFOM (159.4)'s rate; required with volatile > 0, refused with
volatile == 0.

diameter.description:
m, the one diameter of a monodisperse cloud; exactly one of this
and `rosinRammler` states the size.

parcelsPerCell.description: Parcels per cell, the K of (159.12); absent is 1.

rosinRammler.description:
The Rosin-Rammler law of (147.1): `d` is d_bar, its size parameter
X; `n` is the spread q.

limitOmegaProduction.description:
(156.8)'s limiter on the ω production; the default is false, the
tree's kinematic behaviour (§156.3).

sust.description: SST-sust's ambient state (156.9); absent is off.

kAmb.description: m²/s², the ambient turbulent kinetic energy.

cfl.description: The largest fraction of `d^2` one sub-step may remove (76.10).

JsonExact.description: Interchange with the polyhedra preserved - SPEC-LIT S44.1.

format.description:
`vtu` or `openfoam` (`foam`), or a comma list. A volume format is an
error naming `visualisation`.

interval.description:
Seconds of physical time between writes; absent is "once, at the
end" - SPEC-LIT S44.4.

precision.description:
**Always a SPEC-LIT S44.3 error.** Present as a field, rather than
left to `deny_unknown_fields`, so the message can say *why* - a lossy
"exact" format is a contradiction in the name - and name
`visualisation.precision`, where reduced precision belongs.

PrtModel.description:
SPEC-LIT S37.4: which closure supplies `Pr_t` in S26's
`k_eff = k + rho cp nu_t/Pr_t` - `"constant"` (the default, and what
`Prt` above means on its own) or `"KaysCrawford"` (where `Prt` above
is read as `Pr_t_inf`, the free-stream asymptote). A free string
rather than an enum, for the same reason `turbulence.model` is one:
an unrecognised spelling has to reach [`crate::energy::PrtModel::parse`]
and come back as a S13.4 error NAMING the alternatives, not as
serde's "unknown variant".

beta.description:
Thermal expansion coefficient [1/K] - read only under
`physics.buoyancy "boussinesq"`, SPEC-LIT 121.7. There is no default:
`1/T_ref` is the ideal-gas value, a liquid's is an order of magnitude
smaller, and the reader is not entitled to pick one.

rheology.description:
SPEC-LIT §38.7: which closure supplies the LAMINAR viscosity, and its
coefficients. Absent means `Newtonian`, which is `nu` above and is
bitwise the pre-§38 momentum equation.

JsonFreestream.description:
A `farfield` or `supersonicInlet` rule's stated state (SPEC-LIT §122.6):
`p` is GAUGE, in the `p` field's datum (§122.2), `T` in kelvin.

JsonGamg.description:
A rule's `gamg` block (SPEC-LIT 141.7): the keys of an OpenFOAM GAMG
entry this solver honours, each optional. OpenFOAM's `mergeLevels` and
`agglomerator` are not keys here; `deny_unknown_fields` refuses them by
name with the accepted keys as the menu.

cacheAgglomeration.description: Keep the hierarchy while the matrix is unchanged (default true).

maxLevels.description: The most levels, the finest counted (default 50, at least 1).

nCellsInCoarsestLevel.description: Coarsening stops at or below this many cells (default 64, at least 1).

JsonGrading.description:
[`JsonMesh::grading`]'s three optional per-axis entries. A missing axis is
uniform; a present one is validated and lowered by
[`apply_axis_grading`].

JsonGradingAxis.description:
One axis's worth of [`crate::blockgen::GradedAxis`] grading:
`expansion` is the ratio `GradedAxis::expansion` documents (last cell over
first for one-sided, centre over wall for `twoSided`) and must be
strictly positive - `0` or negative is not a cell-size ratio for any
mesh, checked in [`apply_axis_grading`] rather than left for `blockgen` to
silently degenerate to uniform (`GradedAxis::default`'s own `!(r > 0)`
guard exists so a bad ratio never produces NaN coordinates, not so a bad
case file goes unnoticed - SPEC-LIT §13.4).

twoSided.description:
`true`: grade symmetrically toward BOTH ends of the axis (a channel's
two walls); `false` (the default - most cases graded toward only one
end, e.g. a pipe's single wall or a boundary layer growing off one
plate, name that explicitly rather than leaving it to a default that
silently picks a physical setup for them): one-sided, `hi`'s cell
`expansion` times `lo`'s.

JsonIgnition.description:
`combustion.ignition`, the source of (155.4) (SPEC-LIT §155.3). `sigmaT`
omitted is t0 (§151.7 item 8).

W0.description: W_0, 1/s (H20 §3.3's 1e13). Required, finite and above zero.

point.description: The ignition point in world coordinates, m. Required.

sigmaR.description: sigma_r, m (H20 §3.3's 0.25 mm). Required, finite and above zero.

sigmaT.description: sigma_t, s; omitted is t0 (§151.7 item 8).

t0.description:
t_0, s - the end of the ramp and the origin of t_fd. Required, finite
and at or above zero.

T.description:
Absent for an isothermal case - not every case solves a temperature
equation, and a `0` here would claim one does.

k.description:
The four turbulence closure fields, each absent when the case does
not solve it - same reasoning as [`Self::t`]. Present exactly when a
`patches[]` rule must carry the matching [`TurbBc`] - see
[`turb_field_spec`].

regions.description:
SPEC-LIT 125.8.1: `initial.regions`, the boxes that override `U`, `p`
and/or `T` in the cells whose centre lies in them. Only
`ofgpu-compressible` applies them, and [`JsonCase::lower`] refuses
them on a case without `physics.compressible`. Absent means uniform.

JsonInitialRegion.description:
One `initial.regions` entry (SPEC-LIT 125.8.1): a box of cell centres,
each stated field overriding the uniform `initial` value in the cells
whose centre falls inside it. Only `ofgpu-compressible` applies a region.

T.description:
The temperature the region's cells take, absent keeps `initial.T`.
Requires `initial.T` on the case - the gas law has no state without
one to override.

U.description: The velocity the region's cells take, absent keeps `initial.U`.

box.description: The cell-centre box, in mesh coordinates, closed on both ends.

p.description: The gauge pressure the region's cells take, absent keeps `initial.p`.

JsonInjector.description:
One `parcels.injectors[]` entry - an `Injector`. `position` and
`massFlow` are required; every other field is `Injector::default()`'s.

JsonIsaac.description:
`output.visualisation.isaac` - SPEC-LIT 117.9's nine keys, `field`
required, the rest optional. Resolved, and every 117.12 refusal raised,
by [`crate::io::output_plan::OutputPlan::from_json`]; nothing here
validates.

Km.description:
Specific extinction, m^2/kg (`physical`); absent is 8700 - 117.14's
8.7 m^2/g of Mulholland & Croarkin 2000.

field.description: The cell field the density is made from. Required.

metersPerUnit.description: The stage's unit scale; absent is 1.0.

range.description:
`[f_lo, f_hi]` of the normalisation (`opticalDepth`); absent is the
min and max of the field over the fluid voxels.

tau.description:
The target optical depth of the densest column (`opticalDepth`);
absent is 2.0.

upAxis.description: The stage's up axis; absent is `"Z"`.

snGrad.description:
The `snGradSchemes` half of a `laplacianSchemes` entry -
`crate::io::schemes::parse_sn_grad`'s grammar (`corrected`,
`uncorrected`, `limited <alpha>`). The `Gauss <interpolation>` half is
not exposed: `linear` is the only interpolation this solver has, so
there is nothing for a case to choose.

JsonLattice.description:
`output.visualisation.lattice` - SPEC-LIT 117.3's six keys, every one
optional. Resolved, and every 117.12 refusal raised, by
[`crate::io::output_plan::OutputPlan::from_json`]; nothing here
validates.

background.description: The value of a voxel no cell claims; absent is `0.0`.

box.description:
`[xlo, ylo, zlo, xhi, yhi, zhi]`, metres. Absent is the bounding box
of the mesh points.

maxVoxels.description:
The voxel budget; absent is 8 000 000. An explicit `voxel` the
budget would coarsen more than 16 times is refused (117.3).

voxel.description:
The voxel edge `h`, in metres; voxels are cubes. Absent is
`(min_c V_c)^(1/3)`, the cube root of the smallest cell volume.

JsonLiquid.description:
`parcels.evaporation.liquid` - a preset (`water`, the default, or
`benzene`) and any of its nine properties overridden.

cyclic.description:
SPEC-LIT §31.1: cyclic pairs, each naming two of the six `boundaries`
values. Empty (the default) is the ordinary, uncoupled mesh this
reader has always built. See [`JsonCyclicPair`].

grading.description:
Per-axis grading toward the axis's own two ends, lowered onto
[`crate::blockgen::GradedAxis`] exactly as `blockgen`'s own cases use
it (`src/blockgen.rs`'s `case_block_spec`, e.g. the channel case's
`b.y.expansion = 20.0; b.y.two_sided = true;`). Absent entirely, or an
axis absent from it, keeps that axis uniform - the pre-grading
behaviour this reader had before, bit for bit (see
`a_case_without_grading_lowers_to_the_same_mesh_as_before`).

sector.description:
SPEC-LIT 157.3: presence makes the case a 1-D SPHERICAL SECTOR - the
REDUCED dust gates' mesh (DST-07). The x axis is the radius
(`bounds.max[0]` = R, `cells[0]` the uniform cell count), `xmin`
names the APEX, which has no faces exactly like a wedge pipe's axis,
`xmax` the outer square and ymin/ymax/zmin/zmax the four sides. The
reader lowers the case onto `crate::dust::gatemesh::SectorSpec` and
refuses everything a sector mesh cannot say (each a §13.4 error
naming the JSON path and SPEC-LIT 157.3). Absent: the case lowers
exactly as before.

wedge.description:
SPEC-LIT 119.3: presence makes the case a WEDGE - the block is the
(r, z) block of the 119.0 mesh (`x` the radius, `z` the axis through
`x = 0, y = 0`, `y` the one-cell circumferential direction) and
`angle` is the FULL wedge angle in degrees, stated once, here. The
reader lowers the case onto `crate::blockgen::WedgeSpec` and refuses
everything a wedge mesh cannot say (its refusal list, each a §13.4
error naming the JSON path and this section). Absent: the case
lowers exactly as before, and no boundary may resolve to a `wedge`
rule - a box has no wedge sides.

JsonMotion.description:
The `motion` block - SPEC-LIT 105.12. One rule per boundary patch (every
patch of the mesh named exactly once, which `MeshMotion::new` checks) and
the `move` patches whose velocity condition is the moving wall's.

div.description:
`divSchemes`, keyed by entry name (`"default"`, `"div(phi,U)"`, ...).
A map rather than named fields: the set of equations a case names here
is open-ended, and `crate::io::schemes::parse_div` is what validates
each value, not this type.

solvers.description:
ORDERED, matched first-to-last against the equation's name - the same
reason `patches` is an array rather than a map.

JsonOutput.description:
What this run writes: three sub-blocks, three purposes - SPEC-LIT S44.

This block was a S13.4 refusal in its entirety until S44, and the reason
is worth keeping: three of its knobs (`visualisation.fields`,
`visualisation.precision`, `restart.keep`) had no implementation anywhere
in the crate, so honouring `format` and `interval` because they happened
to exist and dropping the other three in silence would have manufactured
S13.4.1's own defect inside its fix. S44 builds all three
([`crate::io::output_plan::FieldSelection`],
[`crate::io::nvdb::Precision`] on both volume writers, and
[`crate::restart::Checkpoints`]) and then honours the block whole.

Resolution, and every S13.4 refusal, is
[`crate::io::output_plan::OutputPlan::from_json`]. A case that carries
this block must NOT also name `-output`/`-writeInterval`/`-restartWrite`
on the command line: those are the same settings said twice, and naming
both is an error rather than a silent winner (S44.6).

JsonParcels.description:
The `parcels` block. Every key but `capacity` and `injectors` is optional,
and an absent key is the library's `Default` (SPEC-LIT §137.2), except
where §137.6 says otherwise.

cLiquid.description: J/(kg K); read by `heating` and `evaporating` only.

cfl.description: The motion sub-step's fraction of a cell (66.7).

coupling.description: SPEC-LIT §68.6 and §77; absent is no coupling at all.

cpGas.description: J/(kg K); read by `heating` and `evaporating` only.

gravity.description: m/s2. Absent: the case's `physics.gravity` on the JSONC route.

injectors.description: One entry per nozzle, at least one (SPEC-LIT §66.8).

kGas.description: W/(m K); read by `heating` and `evaporating` only.

persistentBlocks.description: Blocks in the persistent grid; absent derives it from `capacity`.

restitution.description: Normal restitution, `[0, 1]`; read by `rebound` and `weber` only.

tangentialLoss.description: Tangential loss, `[0, 1]`; read by `rebound` and `weber` only.

wall.description:
`remove` (default) | `rebound` | `stick` | `weber`; `film`, `spread`
and `splash` are refused with their SPEC-LIT §78 reasons.

JsonPatchRule.description: One ordered rule of the `patches` array.

Cs.description:
The roughness constant; defaults to `0.5` (SPEC-LIT §15.3's "uniform
sand") when `Ks` is given and this is not.

Ks.description:
Sand-grain height, m - required when the effective treatment (this
rule's own [`Self::wall_treatment`], or the case default) is `rough`.

freestream.description:
SPEC-LIT §122.6: the state a `farfield` or `supersonicInlet` rule
states, required there and refused on every other kind.

k.description:
`k`'s own condition. Only required when `initial.k` is given (this
case solves `k`) - see [`turb_field_spec`].

treatment.description:
SPEC-LIT §29.1 route (b): this patch's own `wallTreatment` override,
on a `wall`-kind patch only - `None` falls back to
`turbulence.wallTreatment`, the case-level default. Meaningless (and
simply unused) on an `inlet`/`open` rule.

JsonPatchTurbulence.description:
The turbulence intensity/mixing-length estimate an inlet carries, in the
same units OpenFOAM's own `turbulentIntensityKineticEnergyInlet` /
`turbulentMixingLengthDissipationRateInlet` take: `intensity` a fraction
of the inlet speed, `mixingLength` an absolute length in metres (NOT a
fraction - `crate::blockgen`'s canned cases multiply a fraction by a
hydraulic diameter internally; a case file names the length directly).

compressible.description:
SPEC-LIT §122.6: the perfect gas of §122.1. Absent (the default) is
every case this reader has ever built; present, it lowers to
[`LoweredCase::compressible`].

JsonPrescribedUt.description:
`combustion.prescribedUt`, the prescribed burning law of Gate DST-VES
(SPEC-LIT §157.6 (i)): `U_t = S0 (T_u(p)/T_u0)^alpha (p/p0)^beta` with
`T_u(p)/T_u0 = (p/p0)^((g-1)/g)` - a test input, not a correlation
claim. `alpha` and `beta` omitted are 0, the constant law.

S0.description:
m/s, the burning velocity at the initial state. Required, finite
and above zero.

alpha.description: The exponent of the unburned-temperature ratio; omitted is 0.

beta.description: The exponent of the pressure ratio; omitted is 0.

JsonRegion.description:
A rectangular window carved out of one box face, replacing the
`PatchWindow` workaround `docs/05-io-redesign.md` section 4.1's opening
comment complains about: here it is just a region.

on.description:
Which `JsonBoundaries` face this window is cut from: `xmin`, `xmax`,
`ymin`, `ymax`, `zmin` or `zmax`.

JsonRestart.description: This solver's own state, to resume from - SPEC-LIT S44.1/S44.5.

interval.description:
Seconds of physical time between checkpoints; absent is "once, at
the end".

keep.description:
How many checkpoints to retain. `0` keeps every one of them -
SPEC-LIT S44.5, and the safe reading of a zero is the one that
deletes nothing.

precision.description:
**Always a SPEC-LIT S44.3 error**, for a sharper reason than
`exact`'s: S5.1's argument for carrying `phi` in a checkpoint is that
a re-derived flux is not the conservative one, and a rounded one is
not either.

JsonRheology.description:
`physics.fluid.rheology` - SPEC-LIT §38.

Every coefficient is in the literature's DYNAMIC units and the block
carries its own `rho` [kg/m³], because §5's momentum equation is
KINEMATIC and the conversion cannot be guessed (§38.4). `rho` is required
for every non-Newtonian model.

The coefficients are `Option` and the model is a free string on purpose.
The string has to reach [`crate::rheology::RheologyModel::parse`] and come
back as a §13.4 error NAMING the six spellings, not as serde's "unknown
variant"; and the options are what let [`JsonCase::lower`] tell "the case
wrote tau0" from "the case did not", so a coefficient the named model does
not read is REFUSED rather than dropped. That check is
[`crate::rheology::RheologyCoeffs::read_keys`], shared verbatim with the
OpenFOAM reader so there is one §13.4 contract and not two.

gammaDotFloor.description: Floor on `gdot` before any divide or power [1/s] - §38.3.

m.description:
Papanastasiou's regularisation parameter [s] - §38.3. A NUMERICAL
parameter, and printed as one.

muMin.description: Clip on the apparent viscosity [Pa s].

relax.description: Elementwise relaxation of the viscosity fixed point - §38.5(iv).

rho.description: Density [kg/m³] - required for every non-Newtonian model (§38.4).

d.description: m, the size parameter X of (147.1).

adjustTimeStep.description:
`false` (the default) is honoured, because a fixed step is what every
driver that reads a JSONC case does.

`true` is a SPEC-LIT S13.4 ERROR naming the alternatives: no such
driver adjusts its own step. `ofgpu-vof` is the one adaptive loop in
this crate (`controlDict` `adjustTimeStep` + `maxCo`, or `-maxCo`) and
it takes an OpenFOAM case directory. `-permissive` substitutes a fixed
step of `deltaT` and says so.

deltaT.description: The time step. Honoured; `-deltaT` on the command line overrides it.

endTime.description:
The end time the case asks for. Honoured: both case readers turn it
into `TurbulenceControls::n_outer_iterations` (steady) or a step count
(transient). `ofgpu-lowmach` takes its run MODE from `-endTime`/`-deltaT`
instead and prints which of the two is in force (SPEC-LIT S13.4.2).

maxCo.description:
The Courant ceiling an adaptive step would hold. A SPEC-LIT S13.4
ERROR whenever present, for the same reason as `adjustTimeStep`: it
only means anything to a loop that adjusts its step, and no driver
reading this format has one.

JsonSector.description:
[`JsonMesh::sector`]'s one entry - SPEC-LIT 157.3. `angle` is the FULL
angle between opposite side faces in degrees (finite, in `(0, 90]`),
`fineRadius` the uniform spacing's end `r_f` in m (`0 < r_f <
bounds.max[0]`) and `growth` the ratio of successive radial spacings
beyond `r_f` (finite, in `[1, 1.2]`) - each checked with its JSON path
named, in [`JsonCase::lower`].

JsonShape.description:
Internally tagged on `kind`, so today's one variant already carries its
own `oneOf`/`const` discriminator in [`emit_schema`]'s output and a second
shape (`cylinder`, say) is additive.

gamg.description:
The GAMG settings of SPEC-LIT 141.7, allowed only on a rule whose
`solver` or `preconditioner` is `GAMG`. Absent: the cycle's
defaults (SPEC-LIT 141.5) and `cacheAgglomeration` true.

maxIter.description:
`SolverControls::default`'s own `1000` when absent, for the same
reason as [`Self::rel_tol`].

relTol.description:
`SolverControls::default`'s own `0.0` (no relative tolerance) when
absent - the same fallback an OpenFOAM `solvers/<var>` entry with no
`relTol` gets from `read_solver_controls`.

JsonSource.description:
One `sources[]` entry - SPEC-LIT §18's registry, reached from JSONC.

*DESIGN.* `constant/fvSources` (SPEC-LIT §18, [`crate::sources::read_sources`])
already has six term kinds over a box/sphere/all-cells selector; this is
deliberately not a second copy of that whole surface. It exists because a
PERIODIC case (SPEC-LIT §31.1) has no inlet to prescribe a mass flow from,
so the only way left to drive it is a momentum source, and JSONC had no
way to say one at all - not even the uniform, whole-domain case a periodic
channel needs. `momentumSource` is that one case, reusing
[`crate::sources::SourceTerm::BodyForce`] and
[`crate::sources::CellSelector::All`] exactly as the OpenFOAM route would
build them for `selection all`. A JSONC case that wants a ZONED source
(a heat release in a box, say) still has no JSONC way to ask for one -
extending this enum with `box`/`sphere` selectors is future work, not a
gap this closes.

field.description:
Which equation the body force acts on. A body force is a VECTOR
(SPEC-LIT §18's [`crate::sources::SourceTerm::BodyForce`] doc) and
only the momentum equation has a direction for it to point in, so
`"U"` is the only value [`JsonCase::lower`] accepts - present
anyway, spelled out, rather than assumed silently, exactly as the
OpenFOAM `constant/fvSources` route requires a `field` entry.

oneOf.description:
SPEC-LIT §35.1: the bulk-temperature thermostat, a volumetric
proportional controller on the domain's own volume-mean `T`. Always
corrects `T` and always acts over the whole mesh - see
[`crate::sources::Thermostat`]'s own doc for why. `tau` omitted
defaults to the domain's flow-through time
([`crate::sources::flow_through_time`]).

`weighting` (SPEC-LIT §35.3) says how the controller DISTRIBUTES the
total power it asks for: `"uniform"`, the default, spreads it by
volume, and `"massFlux"` spreads it by the local streamwise mass flux
`rho u . e_hat`, which is what the periodic-fully-developed
decomposition actually calls for. `direction` gives `e_hat`; omitted,
it is taken from the mesh's single cyclic pair, and a mesh with none
or with several is a §13.4 error rather than a guess.

direction.description:
SPEC-LIT §35.3.5's `e_hat`. Only meaningful with
`"weighting": "massFlux"`; given alongside `"uniform"` it is a
§13.4 error, since uniform has no direction to use and reading it
and ignoring it is exactly the silent drop §13.4 forbids.

weighting.description:
SPEC-LIT §35.3. Omitted is `"uniform"` - deliberately, so every
measurement already recorded with the uniform form stays
reproducible bit for bit (§35.3.6).

inert.description: The species closed by `1 - sum` (SPEC-LIT §19). No default.

initial.description:
name -> the uniform initial mass fraction of every solved species.
The inert one's is `1 - sum` and is not stated.

names.description: Every species, the inert one included.

JsonSpeciesPatch.description:
One `species.patches[]` rule: the mass-fraction condition of each named
species on every boundary patch `match` matches.

Le.description: name -> Lewis number; 1 for every species not named.

Sct.description: The turbulent Schmidt number; SPEC-LIT §19's 0.7 when absent.

model.description:
`kEpsilon`, `kOmegaSST`, ... - validated at model-construction time,
same as an OpenFOAM `momentumTransport`'s `RAS/model`; not here, so a
build without a given model is not a reason to refuse every case.

wallTreatment.description:
SPEC-LIT §29.1 route (b): the case-level `wallTreatment` default every
wall patch's four turbulence-closure types expand to, unless a patch's
own `treatment` ([`JsonPatchRule::wall_treatment`]) or its own
explicit `k`/`epsilon`/`omega`/`nut` overrides it. `standard` (the
OpenFOAM-compatible default) when the case names none.

JsonVent.description:
The case's `vent` block, `JsonCase::vent` (SPEC-LIT §158.8): a normal and
`pStat`, then either the disc (`centre` + `radius`) or the face set (`faces`).

centre.description: The disc route: a point on the membrane plane, and the disc radius [m].

faces.description: The face-set route: internal face ids of the case's mesh.

normal.description: Points from the inside (the vessel) to the outside; any length > 0.

pStat.description: Pa, the static activation pressure: opens when p_in - p_out >= pStat.

radius.description: The disc route: the radius [m] about `centre`, in the plane.

wall.description: `noSlip` (default) | `slip`: U on the membrane while closed.

JsonVisualisation.description:
The dense voxel grid a renderer reads - SPEC-LIT S44.1.

Resolved by [`crate::io::output_plan::OutputPlan::from_json`], which is
where every S13.4 refusal about these six entries lives; nothing here
validates, exactly as nothing else in this file does.

fields.description:
Which cell fields to write, and in what order. Absent is every field
the run has - SPEC-LIT S44.2.

format.description:
`vdb`, `nvdb`, or a comma list of them. A format from `exact`'s
column (`vtu`, `openfoam`) is an error naming `exact`; `usda` is an
error naming `usdScene`.

interval.description:
Seconds of physical time between writes. Absent (or `0`) is
"the final state, once" - SPEC-LIT S44.4. Was REQUIRED before S44.

isaac.description:
The Isaac Sim profile - SPEC-LIT 117.9: one `density` grid on the
`.vdb` and the `.usda` scene. Absent writes exactly what this crate
has always written.

lattice.description:
The lattice a mesh that is not a uniform Cartesian box is sampled
onto - SPEC-LIT 117.3. Absent is every default of that table. A
uniform Cartesian box is written on its own cells and never reads it.

precision.description:
`fp32` (the default) or `fp16` - SPEC-LIT S44.3. This is the ONE
place in the case format where reduced precision is legitimate.

usdScene.description: Also write a `.usda` scene referencing the volume files.

JsonWedge.description:
[`JsonMesh::wedge`]'s one entry - SPEC-LIT 119.3. `angle` is the FULL
wedge angle in degrees, finite and strictly between 0 and 180 (checked
in [`build_block`], naming this path).

oneOf.description:
SPEC-LIT §34.1: `PatchKind::Empty` - the 2-D "this axis does not
exist" declaration the solver has always understood
(`OFPATCH_EMPTY`), newly nameable in JSONC. A CONSTRAINT, not a
boundary condition: legal only on a slot exactly one cell across
(checked in [`build_block`]), and a rule of this kind may not also
carry a per-field BC (checked in [`validate_constraint_rules`]) -
the constraint decides every field, and `field_setup::topology_override`
would silently win over a per-field BC anyway, so naming one is
always a mistake worth catching rather than a redundancy worth
tolerating.

SPEC-LIT §34.1: `PatchKind::Symmetry` - the mirror-plane constraint
the solver's vector-reflection branch has always understood, newly
nameable in JSONC. Same CONSTRAINT rules as [`Self::Empty`], minus
the single-cell check (a symmetry plane has no such restriction).

SPEC-LIT 119.3: `PatchKind::Wedge` - the third CONSTRAINT kind. Needs
a mesh that has wedge sides (`mesh.wedge`, the 119.0 block): the
reader refuses a `wedge` rule on a mesh without one, and on a wedge
mesh holds `ymin`/`ymax` to a `wedge` rule and every other slot away
from one. Same per-field refusal as [`Self::Empty`] and
[`Self::Symmetry`] - the constraint decides every field,
turbulence fields included - and 119.2's `BcKind::Wedge` is what the
field seed and `field_setup::topology_override` force on its faces.

SPEC-LIT §122.6 and §126.6: the characteristic far field. Its rule
states the free stream (`freestream`), and `U`, `p` and `T` all lower
to `characteristicFarfield` at that state; only in a case with
`physics.compressible`.

SPEC-LIT §122.6 and §126.2: supersonic inflow, `p`, `U` and `T` all
`fixedValue` at the rule's `freestream`; only in a case with
`physics.compressible`.

ScalarBc.description:
One `{"type": "fixedValue", "value": ...}`-shaped scalar boundary
condition. Internally tagged, so `emit_schema` renders it as `oneOf` with
a `const` discriminator on `type` - deliverable 4 of this module.

oneOf.description:
SPEC-LIT §29.3's Jayatilleke thermal wall function, nameable
explicitly on `T` with its own wall target temperature `T_w` -
[`TurbBc`]'s wall-function variants already carry a `value` this same
way for `nut`/`k`/`epsilon`/`omega`; `T` had no such variant, only the
case-level `wallTreatment` auto-completion of [`t_spec_for`], which
(deliberately, until this variant existed) never has a wall
temperature of its own to write and falls back to the neighbour
cell's value - fine for an adiabatic-ish plume floor, useless for a
genuinely hot wall against a cooler bulk (SPEC-LIT §29.3's own
deferred gate: a channel with fixed-T hot walls). An explicit
`T: { "type": "thermalWallFunction", "value": T_w }` on a wall rule is
the highest-precedence route of §29.1's table and is honoured here the
same way an explicit `nutkWallFunction { value }` already is.

SPEC-LIT §32.2's redesigned thermal-wall gate: a wall carrying a fixed
heat FLUX `q` (W/m^2) rather than a temperature -
`crate::field::BcKind::FixedFluxTemperature`. Deliberately the SAME
JSON type on a `wallTreatment: standard` wall-function mesh and a
`lowRe` resolved one - see that `BcKind` variant's own doc for why one
condition is exact on both.

TurbBc.description:
One `k`/`epsilon`/`omega`/`nut` boundary condition. A superset of
[`ScalarBc`]: a turbulence closure field's wall treatment is a wall
FUNCTION, not `fixedValue`/`zeroGradient`, and which one governs whether
[`crate::field_setup::WallFaces::from_case`] treats a patch as a wall at
all (it reads `epsilon`'s and `nut`'s own patch *type strings* - see that
function and `crate::field_setup::wall_cell_faces`/`nut_wall_faces`). This
type exists because the B3 gate (`docs/05-io-redesign.md` phase 1) needs a
JSONC case to reproduce a generated OpenFOAM case's `k`/`epsilon`/`nut`
EXACTLY, wall-function type strings included - `JsonPatchTurbulence`'s
intensity/mixing-length inlet estimate has nothing to say about a wall
patch's type, only an inlet's value. `value` is the uniform value written
on every variant, including the wall-function ones: OpenFOAM itself writes
a `value` entry there too (the field's own initial guess before the wall
function first runs), and `docs/case-example.json`'s own generated
counterpart does the same - see e.g. `cases/plumeB/0/k`'s `floor` entry.

oneOf.description:
`nut`'s own non-wall-function type (an inlet/outlet with no
prescribed eddy viscosity) - OpenFOAM's `calculated`.

SPEC-LIT §15.1/§29.1: `y+` from the local velocity rather than `k` -
an explicit per-patch override of the `spalding` preset row's `nut`,
nameable on its own patch under any case-level default (§29.1's
precedence: "explicit per-field BCs...override").

SPEC-LIT §15.2/§29.1: `nu_t,w = 0`, no wall model - the `lowRe`
preset row's `nut`, nameable explicitly on one patch.

SPEC-LIT §15.4/§29.1: the resolved-sublayer `k` completion - the
`lowRe` preset row's `k`, nameable explicitly on one patch.

WallTreatmentKind.description:
SPEC-LIT §29.1's four presets, as the JSONC format spells them -
`crate::io::case::WallTreatment`'s twin, kept separate so this module's
[`schemars`] derive is what puts the four names in [`emit_schema`]'s
output rather than a hand-written schema fragment that could drift from
the reader.

Word.description: A word the case may write as a string or as a number (`variant 1989`).
